engines.name: AI Engine
engines.description: Async AI Engine + SecureGraph Agent platform (Architecture v1.1): Chief Security Agent orchestrates engines; OpenClaw skills; finding explanations, executive summaries, governance. Never blocks HTTP.
must_not: Block API requests waiting on LLM completion
Write scan results as source of truth
Send customer PII to providers without redaction
Create central lake of tenant security data

engines.name: Asset Engine
engines.description: Asset inventory, discovery, tags, history, integrations, and Asset Intelligence Phase 2 (graph, SSE realtime, AI posture narratives)
must_not: Calculate risk scores (reads Risk Engine scores; does not re-score)
Write audit trail records (publish AuditRecorded via bus)

engines.name: Audit Engine
engines.description: Immutable audit trail of what happened (not who may act)
must_not: Authorize actions (Control Plane owns dual-control sessions/pending queue)
Own dual-control pending action queue (Control Plane)

engines.name: Compliance Engine
engines.description: Database-driven compliance knowledge base, profiling, assessments, and report sections (NDPR/ISO/SOC2/PCI/GDPR)
must_not: Own remediation decisions (Risk Engine treatment statuses)
Store raw Wazuh alerts as system of record without normalization

engines.name: Control Plane
engines.description: Platform management: auth, orgs, billing, licensing, customer setup, staff portal, support
must_not: Execute scans or invoke scanner tools

engines.name: Operations Engine
engines.description: Platform monitoring, process management, optimization, developer logs
must_not: Execute customer-facing scans as product feature

engines.name: Reporting Engine
engines.description: Consolidates engine sections, CVSS enrichment, finding tracker, and multi-format report production (never scans or scores risk)
must_not: Interpret or modify engine section content (preserve as-provided)
Send notifications (publishes events for Alert Engine)
Store raw scan results as system of record
Hold more than REPORT_MAX_VERSIONS reports per type per org

engines.name: Risk Engine
engines.description: Risk scoring, treatments, prioritization, residual risk
must_not: Send channel deliveries (publish events for Alert Engine)
Generate final PDF board reports (Reporting Engine)

engines.name: Scanner Engine
engines.description: Scan orchestration, tool adapters, VAPT workflows, result normalization

engines.name: SOC Engine
engines.description: Security Operations Center: detection correlation, analyst triage, optional cases, realtime monitoring dashboard, availability/uptime probes with MTTR, enrichment adapters, log ingestion pipeline, playbook-driven IR with MITRE ATT&CK kill chain, cloud provider log adapters, AI-powered security advisory
must_not: Author risk scores (Risk Engine owns scoring)
Write customer audit trail without Audit Engine
Invent detections without stored signals or analyst input

engines.name: Threat Model Engine
engines.description: Design surface + Product Context: per-org product projects, components/trust boundaries, flows and documents (draw.io + uploads), evidence-graded stage-aware threat modelling with a clarifying-question loop, exports and delivery to ticketing/risk.
must_not: Store customer context outside the customer security DB
Present unverified findings as confirmed (grade = supported only with evidence)
Block HTTP on LLM calls (async-only AI)

engines.name: VAPT Engine
engines.description: Vulnerability Assessment & Penetration Testing campaigns: multi-step procedures, pause/resume, attack-path correlation, complexity classification for AI gating
must_not: Execute scan tools directly (uses Scanner Engine)
Call LLMs directly (AI Engine via bus)
Store raw tool output (Scanner owns scan_results)

engines.extension_note: Register additional engines via app.engines.registry.register_engine or add app/engines/<id>/ with MANIFEST.
